title: Transformation Geometry: Translations, Reflections and Rotations on a Grid
seo_title: Grade 7 Transformation Geometry Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise, describe and perform transformations with points on a coordinate plane, focusing on reflecting a point in the X-axis or Y-axis, translating a point within and across quadrants; recognise, describe and perform transformations with triangles on squared paper, including translations, reflections and rotations.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 transformation geometry worksheets: coordinates, translations, reflections and rotations on a grid. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Reflect in the y-axis: change the sign of x.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A point is written (x; y) or (x, y): across first, then up or down.
  • Translation: every point moves the same distance in the same direction.
  • Reflection in the x-axis changes the sign of y; in the y-axis it changes the sign of x.
  • Rotation of 180° about the origin changes both signs.

Examples

Example

Reflect (3, −2) in the y-axis

change the sign of x

Answer: (−3, −2)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong way roundx first, then y.
The wrong axisReflecting in the x-axis changes y.
The wrong directionCheck clockwise or anti-clockwise.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 7 say about transformations?
faq.a: Recognise, describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations with geometric figures and shapes on squared paper, and use the coordinate grid.

faq.q: Does a transformation change the size?
faq.a: Translations, reflections and rotations do not.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 3, then up 5. Point A is at (3, 5). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 4, then up 2. Point B is at (−4, 2). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 2, then down 6. Point C is at (−2, −6). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down. (−6, −2) is point D: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 5, then down 3. Point E is at (5, −3). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point F?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 5, then up 4. Point F is at (−5, 4). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down. (4, −5) is point G: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point H?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 6, then down 1. Point H is at (6, −1). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point J?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 3, then down 3. Point J is at (−3, −3). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then up 4. Point K is at (0, 4). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down. (4, 0) is point L: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 1, then up 6. Point M is at (−1, 6). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point N?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 6, then 0 up or down. Point N is at (−6, 0). Write the x-coordinate first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (4, 2) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (4, 2) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−3, 5) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−3, 5) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−1, −6) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−1, −6) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (5, −4) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (5, −4) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−6, 3) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−6, 3) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (2, −1) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (2, −1) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (6, 6) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (6, 6) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−4, −2) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−4, −2) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants go anti-clockwise from the top right: I, II, III, IV.

items.q: Where is the point (0, 5)?
items.e: x = 0, so the point does not move left or right. It goes up 5 along the y-axis. A point on an axis is not in any quadrant.

items.q: Where is the point (3, 0)?
items.e: y = 0, so the point does not move up or down. It goes right 3 along the x-axis. It is not in any quadrant.

items.q: The point (−3, 3) is translated 2 units right and 1 unit down. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving right changes the x-coordinate by 2; moving down changes the y-coordinate by −1. Image: (−1, 2).

items.q: The point (3, 5) is translated 5 units right and 1 unit down. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving right changes the x-coordinate by 5; moving down changes the y-coordinate by −1. Image: (8, 4).

items.q: The point (2, −2) is translated 1 unit left and 4 units up. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving left changes the x-coordinate by −1; moving up changes the y-coordinate by 4. Image: (1, 2).

items.q: The point (2, 4) is translated to (−3, −2). Describe the translation.
items.e: x: 2 → −3 is −5. y: 4 → −2 is −6. 5 units left and 6 units down.

items.q: The point (2, −2) is translated 6 units right and 1 unit up. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving right changes the x-coordinate by 6; moving up changes the y-coordinate by 1. Image: (8, −1).

items.q: The point (0, 4) is translated 1 unit left and 6 units down. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving left changes the x-coordinate by −1; moving down changes the y-coordinate by −6. Image: (−1, −2).

items.q: The point (2, −5) is translated to (7, −2). Describe the translation.
items.e: x: 2 → 7 is 5. y: −5 → −2 is 3. 5 units right and 3 units up.

items.q: The point (−4, 4) is translated to (−2, 7). Describe the translation.
items.e: x: −4 → −2 is 2. y: 4 → 7 is 3. 2 units right and 3 units up.

items.q: The point (−1, 0) is translated to (1, −4). Describe the translation.
items.e: x: −1 → 1 is 2. y: 0 → −4 is −4. 2 units right and 4 units down.

items.q: The point (4, 3) is translated 5 units left and 6 units down. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving left changes the x-coordinate by −5; moving down changes the y-coordinate by −6. Image: (−1, −3).

items.q: Translate (3, −2) 6 units left. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 6 units left: x: 3 − 6 = −3, y stays −2. (3, −2) → (−3, −2).

items.q: Translate (−1, 4) 7 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 7 units down: x stays −1, y: 4 − 7 = −3. (−1, 4) → (−1, −3).

items.q: Translate (−5, −3) 8 units right. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 8 units right: x: −5 + 8 = 3, y stays −3. (−5, −3) → (3, −3).

items.q: Translate (−3, 2) 5 units right and 4 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 5 units right and 4 units down: x: −3 + 5 = 2, y: 2 − 4 = −2. (−3, 2) → (2, −2).

items.q: Translate (4, −1) 6 units left and 3 units up. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 6 units left and 3 units up: x: 4 − 6 = −2, y: −1 + 3 = 2. (4, −1) → (−2, 2).

items.q: Translate (−2, −5) 7 units right and 4 units up. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 7 units right and 4 units up: x: −2 + 7 = 5, y: −5 + 4 = −1. (−2, −5) → (5, −1).

items.q: Translate (5, 3) 3 units left and 7 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 3 units left and 7 units down: x: 5 − 3 = 2, y: 3 − 7 = −4. (5, 3) → (2, −4).

items.q: Point P is translated 6 units right and 3 units down. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (−5, 2). Translate 6 units right and 3 units down: x: −5 + 6 = 1, y: 2 − 3 = −1. (−5, 2) → (1, −1). That is point B. Point C moves the wrong way up or down, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 units left and 3 units up. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (4, −2). Translate 6 units left and 3 units up: x: 4 − 6 = −2, y: −2 + 3 = 1. (4, −2) → (−2, 1). That is point A. Point C moves the wrong way up or down, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 units left and 2 units down. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (3, 4). Translate 5 units left and 2 units down: x: 3 − 5 = −2, y: 4 − 2 = 2. (3, 4) → (−2, 2). That is point C. Point B moves the wrong way up or down, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: The point (3, −1) is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−3, −1).

items.q: The point (4, 0) is reflected in the line x = 1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−2, 0).

items.q: The point (−5, −2) is reflected in the line y = −1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (−5, 0).

items.q: The point (−4, 3) is reflected in the line x = 1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (6, 3).

items.q: The point (−1, 5) is reflected in the line y = 2. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (−1, −1).

items.q: The point (3, 1) is reflected in the line y = −2. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (3, −5).

items.q: The point (3, 4) is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (3, −4).

items.q: The point (5, 0) is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−5, 0).

items.q: The point (−3, 5) is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (−3, −5).

items.q: The point (4, −2) is reflected in the line x = −2. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−8, −2).

items.q: Reflect (5, −3) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (5, −3) → (−5, −3).

items.q: Reflect (−2, 6) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−2, 6) → (−2, −6).

items.q: Reflect (4, 1) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (4, 1) → (4, −1).

items.q: Reflect (−6, −4) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−6, −4) → (6, −4).

items.q: Reflect (−1, −5) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−1, −5) → (−1, 5).

items.q: Reflect (2, 3) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (2, 3) → (−2, 3).

items.q: Reflect (0, −5) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (0, −5) is on the y-axis (the mirror line), so it stays at (0, −5).

items.q: Reflect (−3, 0) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−3, 0) is on the x-axis, 3 units left of the y-axis. Reflect in the y-axis: x changes sign, −3 → 3. The image is 3 units right: (3, 0).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−3, 4). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−3, 4) → (−3, −4). That is point A. Point B is the reflection in the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (5, −2). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (5, −2) → (−5, −2). That is point B. Point A is the reflection in the x-axis instead.

items.q: The point (−2, −4) is rotated 180° about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−1, −6) from the centre becomes (1, 6). Image: (0, 8).

items.q: The point (2, −3) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Rotating 180° about the origin changes both signs. Image: (−2, 3).

items.q: The point (−4, 2) is rotated 180° about the point (2, 0). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−6, 2) from the centre becomes (6, −2). Image: (8, −2).

items.q: The point (2, −4) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Rotating 180° about the origin changes both signs. Image: (−2, 4).

items.q: The point (2, 3) is rotated 90° clockwise about the point (2, 0). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (0, 3) from the centre becomes (3, 0). Image: (5, 0).

items.q: The point (−3, −4) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−3, −4) from the centre becomes (−4, 3). Image: (−4, 3).

items.q: The point (3, −4) is rotated 90° clockwise about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (4, −6) from the centre becomes (−6, −4). Image: (−7, −2).

items.q: The point (2, 3) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the point (2, 0). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (0, 3) from the centre becomes (−3, 0). Image: (−1, 0).

items.q: The point (−2, 3) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Rotating 180° about the origin changes both signs. Image: (2, −3).

items.q: The point (2, −2) is rotated 180° about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (3, −4) from the centre becomes (−3, 4). Image: (−4, 6).

items.q: Rotate (2, 5) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (2, 5) → (5, −2).

items.q: Rotate (−3, 1) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−3, 1) → (1, 3).

items.q: Rotate (−4, −6) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−4, −6) → (−6, 4).

items.q: Rotate (5, −2) 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (5, −2) → (2, 5).

items.q: Rotate (1, 3) 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (1, 3) → (−3, 1).

items.q: Rotate (−6, 4) 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (−6, 4) → (−4, −6).

items.q: Rotate (3, −4) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 180°: both signs change. (3, −4) → (−3, 4).

items.q: Rotate (−5, −1) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 180°: both signs change. (−5, −1) → (5, 1).

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (5, 2). Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (5, 2) → (2, −5). That is point C. Point A is a turn the wrong way, and point B only swaps the numbers.

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (−2, 4). Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (−2, 4) → (−4, −2). That is point D. Point A is a turn the wrong way, and point B only swaps the numbers.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 3), B(3, 3), C(1, 6). It is translated 2 units right and 3 units up. What are the coordinates of B′?
items.e: B(3, 3) is translated 2 units right and 3 units up, so B′ is (5, 6).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 1), B(4, 1), C(2, 3). It is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(2, 1) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin, so A′ is (1, −2).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 3), B(5, 3), C(2, 6). It is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(2, 3) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin, so A′ is (3, −2).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 1), B(5, 1), C(3, 4). It is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(3, 1) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin, so A′ is (1, −3).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 3), B(4, 3), C(2, 5). It is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(2, 5) is reflected in the y-axis, so C′ is (−2, 5).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 3), B(3, 3), C(1, 6). It is translated 2 units right and 3 units up. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(1, 6) is translated 2 units right and 3 units up, so C′ is (3, 9).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 1), B(6, 1), C(3, 3). It is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(3, 3) is reflected in the y-axis, so C′ is (−3, 3).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 3), B(4, 3), C(1, 5). It is translated 5 units left and 2 units up. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(1, 3) is translated 5 units left and 2 units up, so A′ is (−4, 5).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 1), B(5, 1), C(2, 4). It is rotated 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(2, 4) is rotated 180° about the origin, so C′ is (−2, −4).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 3), B(6, 3), C(3, 6). It is rotated 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(3, 3) is rotated 180° about the origin, so A′ is (−3, −3).

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Triangle B points the same way as triangle A: it only slid. That is a translation (6 units right and 5 units down). A reflection or a 180° turn would flip or turn the triangle.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (−2, 1) → (2, 1). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−2, 1) → (2, 1). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a reflection in the y-axis.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (5, 1) → (−5, −1). Rotate 180°: both signs change. (5, 1) → (−5, −1). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a rotation of 180°.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (−2, 1) → (1, 2). Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−2, 1) → (1, 2). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a rotation of 90° clockwise.

items.q: Triangle PQR has vertices (2, 1), (5, 1), (5, 3). Its image has vertices (−2, 1), (−5, 1), (−5, 3), in the same order. Which single transformation was used?
items.e: Compare each vertex with its image. Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (2, 1) → (−2, 1). The rule works for every vertex, so it is a reflection in the y-axis.

items.q: Triangle PQR has vertices (−1, 2), (−1, 5), (−3, 5). Its image has vertices (2, 1), (5, 1), (5, 3), in the same order. Which single transformation was used?
items.e: Compare each vertex with its image. Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−1, 2) → (2, 1). The rule works for every vertex, so it is a rotation of 90° clockwise.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices (−3, 2), (−1, 2), (−1, 5). Its image has vertices (3, −1), (1, −1), (1, 2), in the same order. Which combination maps the triangle onto its image?
c: Reflect in the y-axis, then translate 3 units up
Reflect in the x-axis, then translate 3 units down
Reflect in the y-axis, then translate 3 units down
Translate 3 units down, then reflect in the x-axis
items.e: Test it on one vertex. Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−3, 2) → (3, 2). Translate 3 units down: x stays 3, y: 2 − 3 = −1. (3, 2) → (3, −1). The other vertices work the same way.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices (1, 2), (4, 2), (4, 4). Its image has vertices (4, −2), (1, −2), (1, −4), in the same order. Which combination maps the triangle onto its image?
c: Rotate 180° about the origin, then translate 5 units left
Reflect in the y-axis, then translate 5 units right
Translate 5 units right, then rotate 180° about the origin
Rotate 180° about the origin, then translate 5 units right
items.e: Test it on one vertex. Rotate 180°: both signs change. (1, 2) → (−1, −2). Translate 5 units right: x: −1 + 5 = 4, y stays −2. (−1, −2) → (4, −2). The other vertices work the same way.

items.q: Kyle draws a cedar tree beside a lake. The shoreline is the x-axis, and the top of the tree is at (−2, 5). He draws the tree’s reflection in the water. Where is the top of the reflection?
items.e: The water line is the x-axis, so reflect in the x-axis: x stays −2, y changes sign. (−2, 5) → (−2, −5).

items.q: Fatima makes a quilt square for a class display. A triangle piece has a vertex at (1, 4). She rotates the piece 90° clockwise about the centre of the square (the origin) to place the next piece. Where is the vertex now?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (1, 4) → (4, −1).
